questions.question: What is the core trust invariant of a production knowledge graph?
options: Every node must have a human-readable name.
Every accepted node and edge remains traceable to evidence, policy, and time.
Every query must traverse at least three hops.
The language model decides which extracted facts are true.
questions.explanation: Traceable provenance and policy let operators verify, retract, authorize, and reproduce graph claims. A readable label or model confidence is not enough.

questions.question: An aggressive identity policy merges two different employees because their names are similar. What is the most dangerous downstream effect?
options: The graph has one fewer display label.
Relationships from one person can be transferred to the other canonical entity.
Every graph query becomes slower.
The source records are automatically corrected.
questions.explanation: A false merge contaminates the canonical node with the other record's skills, ownership, permissions, and history.

questions.question: Why can a very conservative identity threshold also reduce answer quality?
options: It creates duplicate entity islands that split paths and history.
It converts every relationship into an undirected edge.
It removes provenance from accepted facts.
It makes authorization unnecessary.
questions.explanation: Missed matches leave observations of the same real entity disconnected, so queries see incomplete neighborhoods and broken paths.

questions.question: A question needs a two-edge ownership path, but retrieval is limited to one hop. What should the system do?
options: Guess the owner from the first service name.
Increase depth without a limit until an owner appears.
Report that the path is incomplete or run a separately authorized bounded query.
Ask the language model to invent the missing relationship.
questions.explanation: A bounded query should not claim an answer it did not retrieve. It can abstain or explicitly execute a policy-approved deeper traversal.

questions.question: A complete graph path ends in a restricted compliance document the requester cannot read. Which behavior preserves the access boundary?
options: Generate the answer but hide the citation.
Treat graph membership as permission to reveal the result.
Prune the unsupported path for that requester and abstain or route to an authorized workflow.
Copy the restricted fact into an unrestricted node property.
questions.explanation: Authorization must be enforced during traversal and evidence assembly. Hiding a citation does not make its protected conclusion safe to disclose.

questions.question: Which metric set best separates graph construction problems from answer-generation problems?
options: Only end-user thumbs-up rate.
Node count and total storage size only.
Identity errors, relation precision, path coverage, citation support, and answer correctness by stage.
Average prompt length and model parameter count.
questions.explanation: Stage-specific metrics preserve attribution: they show whether a failure began in identity resolution, edge admission, retrieval, evidence gating, or generation.
